title: Radiomic phenotype features predict pathological response in non-small cell lung cancer

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Radiomic phenotype features predict pathological response in non-small cell lung cancer》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Background and purpose · abstract-1-1】Radiomics can quantify tumor phenotype characteristics non-invasively by applying advanced imaging feature algorithms. In this study we assessed if pre-treatment radiomics data are able to predict pathological response after neoadjuvant chemoradiation in patients with locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Radiomic phenotype features predict pathological response in non-small cell lung cancer》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Materials and methods · abstract-2-1】127 NSCLC patients were included in this study. Fifteen radiomic features selected based on stability and variance were evaluated for its power to predict pathological response. Predictive power was evaluated using area under the curve (AUC). Conventional imaging features (tumor volume and diameter) were used for comparison.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Radiomic phenotype features predict pathological response in non-small cell lung cancer》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Results · abstract-3-1】Seven features were predictive for pathologic gross residual disease (AUC>0.6, p-value<0.05), and one for pathologic complete response (AUC=0.63, p-value=0.01). No conventional imaging features were predictive (range AUC=0.51-0.59, p-value>0.05). Tumors that did not respond well to neoadjuvant chemoradiation were more likely to present a rounder shape (spherical disproportionality, AUC=0.63, p-value=0.009) and heterogeneous texture (LoG 5mm 3D - GLCM entropy, AUC=0.61, p-value=0.03).

【Conclusion · abstract-4-1】We identified predictive radiomic features for pathological response, although no conventional features were significantly predictive. This study demonstrates that radiomics can provide valuable clinical information, and performed better than conventional imaging features.
